key_insight: Trajectory replay updates continuous-time generative models by matching historical and new-task velocity fields, preserving past knowledge without repeatedly generating full replay trajectories.
engineering_relevance: The approach could support continual updating of generative engineering models, but the abstract reports no solid-mechanics or constitutive-modeling validation.
method: Match a frozen historical velocity field along its trajectories and the incoming task’s velocity field.
Use a stability–plasticity coefficient to balance retention and adaptation, yielding density-weighted transport of mixed probability paths.
Apply mean velocity distillation to access historical trajectories with few network evaluations per update.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improvements over generative replay and distillation baselines on class-incremental image generation, plus two biological case studies across two modalities that preserve treatment-effect prediction.
watch_item: Engineering deployment would require validation of physical consistency and sensitivity to the stability–plasticity coefficient.
paper_title: Trajectory Replay: Continuous-Time Mixture Transport for Lifelong Generative Models
